headline: AI Panic Meets the Evidence Gap
thesis: As districts debate AI bans, new reporting says the evidence base for AI in education is still almost nonexistent.
summary: EdSurge asks whether blanket AI bans will cost kids early-literacy support, while its podcast with EdReports probes whether vendor AI claims hold up. Inside Higher Ed reports on Educause's 2027 Top 10, where AI value tops the list for the first time, and quotes MIT's Justin Reich that the research base is "almost nonexistent." THE Journal covers OpenAI retiring Custom GPTs and Microsoft's redesigned Copilot, while EdTech Magazine looks at the true cost of student devices. Ahead: EdTech Week (NYC, Oct 12-16) and the 1EdTech Technical Congress (Oct 19-21).
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · October 7, 2026 · Items come from search-indexed results rather than direct site fetches; several sources had no new dated news and list evergreen items. EdTech Week dates vary by listing (expo Oct 12-16 per latest search).
